findings.title: "act verifier" / "state verifier" and the HONORED/LINE-ONLY verdict vocabulary are used with no definition anywhere in the source
locations: src/CLI/Demote.jl:6-9: "The one demotion rule over an act verdict — the act verifier's grade of what the fix pass DID to one finding, from the diff (the state verifier grades, blind to the diff, whether the defect is still there). `class_surfaces` is the list the verifier fills…"
src/CLI/Demote.jl:11-12: "An act verdict `HONORED` becomes `LINE-ONLY` when that list is empty…"
src/CLI/Passes.jl:283-285 (pass_scope): "An id the previous pass left `pending_state` — graded by the act verifier, never read by the blind one — is a suspect too…"

src/CLI/Passes.jl:587-591 (grade): "applies the demotion to the rest, then the closure channels per id — `honored`, `adjudicated`, `seeded`, `rescan`… A re-checked id — closed earlier, back in scope — keeps the act verdict that closed it…"
findings.description: A cold reader meets `?GBGCodingTools.demote` (Demote.jl is included right after Doctor.jl, well before Passes.jl) and is immediately handed four unglossed terms of art at once: "act verdict", "the act verifier" (vs. "the state verifier", elsewhere called "the blind verifier" — three names for what turn out to be two roles), "class_surfaces", and "swept". None is a plain-English read: an "act verifier" does not mean a verifier that acts, and "swept" here means specifically "a location a finding names that the fix pass's diff touched" (RULE.DOC.CLASS_SWEEP's sense), not the ordinary sense used two lines earlier in Reflection.jl ("whose `src` surface names the files swept", meaning merely "read"). The closed verdict vocabulary itself — `HONORED`, `LINE-ONLY`, and later `PHANTOM`/`UNFIXED`/`ABSENT`/`NOT-A-DEFECT` (Witnesses.jl, Passes.jl) — is never enumerated or explained as a vocabulary anywhere a `?name` lookup would land; each docstring just uses the members as already-known constants. I verified this is not merely a link I missed: I grepped the whole `src/` and `ext/` tree for "act verifier", "state verifier", "blind verifier", "class_surfaces", "HONORED", "LINE-ONLY" and every occurrence is inside a docstring or comment that USES the term, none DEFINES it (the closest thing to a definition, RULE.INST.SELF_REPORT's "the act verifier sees the diff, the state verifier is blind", lives only in the policy rulebook, which a `?name` REPL read never surfaces). By contrast, every other overloaded-but-central term in this package (`consumer`, `instrument`, `round`, `lane`, `hat`, `gate`, the three senses of `anchor`, `surface`, `managed file`, DEAD/REJECTED/EMPTY/TRUNCATED lane statuses) gets exactly this kind of module-docstring or first-use definition elsewhere in the same corpus, which is what makes its absence here conspicuous rather than a house style.
findings.resolution_hint: Bind "act verifier"/"state verifier" (and retire the third name "blind verifier" in favour of whichever the module docstring uses) once, either in the `GBGCodingTools` module docstring alongside `instrument`/`round`/`lane`/`gate`, or in the `Passes` module docstring (which already introduces `demote`, `grade`, `close`) — then `@ref`-link the first mention in `Demote.jl`'s docstring per RULE.DOC.XLINK. State the closed verdict vocabulary (at minimum HONORED, LINE-ONLY, and the exit-vocabulary PHANTOM/UNFIXED/BROKEN a reader meets soon after in Witnesses.jl) in the same place, and use "swept"/"class_surfaces" only after that anchor exists.

findings.title: "shim" is used at its first two mentions (Main.jl) before any docstring says what a shim is
locations: src/CLI/Main.jl:70-71 (running_dev): "`GBG_DEV` is set (the shim's `--dev` route or `main`'s own flag), or the package directory holds a `.git` entry…"
src/CLI/Main.jl:118-119 (main): "The one entry point of the command line: the shim execs `julia -e 'using GBGCodingTools; exit(GBGCodingTools.main(ARGS))'`…"
findings.description: `running_dev` and `main` are the fourth and fifth docstrings in the whole source (CLI/Main.jl is the first CLI file included), and both lean on "the shim" as an already-known noun — a plain-English word here standing in for one specific artifact (the executable at `bin/gbg`, installed to `~/.local/bin/gbg`). Nothing before this point, and nothing in these two docstrings themselves, says what the shim is; the reader only gets it eleven files later, and even then only by inference from `Install.jl`'s `shim_source()`/`shim_target()` docstrings ("The path of `bin/gbg` inside the running copy — the shim body `gbg install` copies"), which describe where it lives and how it is installed but never state in one sentence "the shim is the small script at `bin/gbg` that execs `julia -e 'using GBGCodingTools; ...'`" — the reader has to assemble that themselves by noticing `main`'s docstring already quoted that exact exec line. This is much lower-stakes than the act/state-verifier gap (the word is generic engineering vocabulary and the surrounding sentence makes the general shape — some wrapper script — inferable immediately), but it is exactly the ordinary-word-with-a-specific-referent pattern the cold read is meant to catch, and it is avoidable: `Install.jl`'s own module-level comment ("the shim and the registered dev checkout") could have been one clause added to `running_dev`'s or `main`'s docstring, or `shim` could `@ref`-link `shim_source` at first mention.
findings.resolution_hint: Add one clause to `running_dev`'s or `main`'s docstring at first use — "the shim (`bin/gbg`, the small script `gbg install` copies to `~/.local/bin/gbg`)" — or `@ref`-link the first "shim" to `[`shim_source`](@ref)`.
